title: Hong Scanner event fact record (VS-3)
description: Immutable fact record for one judged transition (docs/REPLAY_CONTRACT.md section 13). An event is emitted exactly once by the single judgment function step(state, record) and is never mutated afterwards: no post-hoc verification state and no delivery state may be added to it, because a mutated fact changes its bytes and breaks replay byte-identity (section 13.4). Verification is recorded only in the session-level verify output; delivery state lives only in contracts/events/delivery.schema.json.

data_quality.description: Trust the judgment placed in its evidence at emission time. Never upgraded after the fact; degraded evidence stays degraded.

direction.description: Judged candidate direction. Present only for events that judged a direction.

event_id.description: Deterministic content address of this fact; see x-event-id-rule. Exactly 64 lowercase hex digits.

event_type.description: The full transition vocabulary of the contract. The contract defines all event types; an implementation may lag the vocabulary, the vocabulary never depends on the implementation.

evidence_ref.description: Non-empty reference to the recorded evidence the judgment consumed. No input seq value may appear here (section 2: the absolute seq value is never emitted in any artifact); record-backed evidence is addressed by content, for example the sha256 hex of the record's canonical line, or by its declared vendor scope, for example ka10027:stex_tp=1:sort_tp=1.

observed_at.description: When the transition was observed, in the scanner canonical timestamp form YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS+HH:MM (numeric offset, the same form the calendar bounds use; see hs/sub_input.validIso8601Offset).

rank.description: Candidate rank in the judged direction at the observed moment. Present only for rank-bearing events; 1 is the first rank.

rule_id.description: Identifier of the judgment rule that produced this fact; stable across runs and versioned by rule_version.

rule_version.description: Version of the judgment rule that produced this fact.

session_id.description: The session the fact belongs to (in the VS-1 scheme, the session_date).

severity.description: Operational importance of the fact, judged at emission time. Importance is part of the fact; delivery priority decisions may consume it but never change it.

symbol.description: 6-digit KRX code the fact is about. Absent when the fact is not symbol-scoped; the event id's entity is then the wildcard.

x-event-id-rule: event_id is the sha256 digest, lowercase hex, over the UTF-8 bytes of the HCJ canonical serialization of the object {"entity":E,"event_type":T,"rule_id":R,"session_id":S,"transition_seq":Q}. E is the record's symbol when present and the wildcard "*" otherwise; T, R and S are the record's event_type, rule_id and session_id; Q is the input record seq (section 2 envelope) of the record at which the transition was observed. Canonical serialization means the HCJ canonical encoder: object keys in codepoint-ascending order (entity, event_type, rule_id, session_id, transition_seq), no whitespace, integers bare. The rule is therefore a pure function: the same tuple yields the same id, and any differing member, including the recorded position Q, yields a different id. Q itself is never emitted in any artifact (section 2); it enters only this one-way digest, and the record carries no position field. The id is computed at generation time by the same step function on both the live and replay paths; it is not recomputable from the record bytes alone because the record does not carry Q.
x-immutability-rule: The record is an immutable fact and this schema is closed (additionalProperties false): every post-hoc field is rejected. verification_status and any session verification state are rejected everywhere (verification lives in the session-level verify output, never in a record). Delivery-state fields such as state, attempts, error_code, provider_message_id or device_id are rejected in the fact (delivery lives in contracts/events/delivery.schema.json). Writing either family into a fact would mutate its bytes and break replay byte-identity (section 13.4).
x-separation-rule: Three states, three homes, never one field for two of them: importance and trust are fact fields (severity, data_quality, plus the judged direction and rank); verification state is session-level (the verify output); delivery state is operational (contracts/events/delivery.schema.json).
